svg.text: Guidemen — Isolated Slope Measurement
2026-09-18 • follow-up to the roof-shell fix • every indirect measurement route was blocked, so each surface was isolated by collision and bisected
Why every earlier attempt failed
• instance AABBs are sign-blind — a Z range cannot say which end is high
• the shell meshes are not world-aligned; each local +Z maps to a world
horizontal axis, so the instance rotation says nothing about the slope
• vertex readback is blocked: get_vertex_position needs a VertexID that
cannot be constructed (the struct's id property is not settable)
• HitResult fields are protected, so a trace's hit location cannot be read
• the tile component is shared by both tiers, so hiding it isolates neither
What worked
Disable collision on every other roof component, then bisect a line trace
on the boolean alone — 18 iterations resolve a surface to 0.01 cm.
No HitResult fields needed, no geometry needed.
The shells are now slope-correct
Every isolated shell falls monotonically away from the ridge line — the
Back shells fall with |y| (main slopes), the Right shells fall with |x|
(hip ends). That is a correct roof. The shell fix is geometrically sound.
Front and Left shells returned no hit because the fix maps each onto its
mirror partner's footprint — only one of each pair is topmost.
But the tiles disagree with the shells
R1_T0 tiles, along y at x = 0:
The tile surface is flat at about 1852 cm along y, while the R2 shell
under it falls 137 cm over the same span. So on the upper tier the tiles do
not lie on the shells.
Along x the tiles do fall (1851 at x=0 to 1718 at x=1200), which is
consistent with a ridge running along Y — but the ridge bars run along X,
the building's long axis, which is where a ridge belongs on a 31.2 x 11.3 m
pavilion.
The three surfaces do not agree with each other
shells fall with |y| (main slopes) and |x| (hip ends) → a ridge along X
tiles flat along y at x=0, falling along x → a ridge along Y
ridge bars run along X, length 3120 / 2720 cm → a ridge along X
Two of the three say the ridge runs along X, which is also what the pavilion's 31.2 x 11.3 m proportion implies. The tile component is
the outlier, and it is the one component that could not be isolated cleanly: `R1_T0` holds both tiers' tiles, so disabling it removes
both. Its flat-along-y reading at x = 0 is therefore the one measurement in this pass I do not fully trust.
Where this leaves it
The shell fix is verified correct by isolation and is kept. The disagreement between the tiles and the shells on the upper tier is real but not yet
resolved, and it is the likely source of what the screenshot shows. Two views would settle it in seconds — a top-down view and a front or side
elevation — because they show the ridge line and each slope's direction directly, which is exactly what no measurement here could do.
Method note carried forward
The capture harness is still broken, so this pass had no visual review either. Every conclusion above comes from geometry and traces. A user screenshot is
currently the only rendering evidence available on this project — which is why the user, and not the tooling, has now caught two of the three roof defects.
